CRM.one_line: CRM/SaaS suite of record (Sales/Service/Data Cloud/Slack) with high switching costs; Agentforce is the new upsell.
CRM.reason: Core growth has decelerated to ~11% but NTM P/E of 14.4x with 9% FCF yield is cheap for a durable enterprise-software leader; Agentforce/AI monetization is optionality, not yet priced in.

red_flags: extreme valuation vs FCF
DDOG.one_line: Leading cloud observability/monitoring platform with high net-revenue-retention and broad product suite.
DDOG.reason: Real 35.6% revenue growth and strong moat, but 93.9x NTM P/E against a 1.1% FCF yield and only 6.8% street upside means the price already assumes near-flawless multi-year execution; too rich to advance now.

red_flags: regulatory: FHFA directed Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac to accept VantageScore 4.0 (Sep 4, 2026), ending FICO's de facto mortgage-scoring monopoly
FICO.one_line: Analytics/credit-scoring monopoly (FICO Score) plus a growing decisioning-software platform.
FICO.reason: Scores segment (the main growth/margin engine, ~60%+ mortgage-driven) faces multi-year competitive erosion now that VantageScore is mandated as an alternative; stock already down >50% from highs but the core moat that justified the premium is structurally impaired, so this is a disqualifying red flag despite still-strong headline growth and a wide analyst price-target gap.

red_flags: long-run AI/free-filing disintermediation risk to TurboTax (monitor, not confirmed this quarter)
INTU.one_line: TurboTax/QuickBooks/Credit Karma/Mailchimp platform with deep consumer and SMB network effects.
INTU.reason: 13.7% revenue growth, 23.6% ROE and an 8.6% FCF yield against an 11.3x NTM P/E (a steep de-rating from Intuit's historical 25x+) look overdone on the downside; 47% street upside supports advancing pending a closer look at the AI-disruption narrative.

red_flags: valuation priced for perfection
PLTR.one_line: AI/data platform (Gotham/Foundry/AIP) for government and enterprise customers, genuinely hyper-growing.
PLTR.reason: 92.8% revenue growth and strong margins are real, but 88.8x NTM P/E, a 0.5% FCF yield and only 3.1% street upside show the price already assumes years of flawless compounding at these rates; too extended to advance.

red_flags: reported revenue (-6.8%) and EPS (-13.6%) declined YoY - needs verification this is a tough prior-year compare / deal-timing lump in the perpetual-to-SaaS transition rather than genuine ARR deceleration
PTC.one_line: PLM/CAD software (Windchill, Onshape, ServiceMax) for industrial manufacturers with high switching costs.
PTC.reason: 41% margins, 35% ROE and a 6.9% FCF yield at 15.5x NTM P/E are unusually strong for a supposedly declining business, suggesting the headline revenue/EPS drop is a comp or timing issue rather than structural decay; worth full diligence to confirm underlying ARR trend before relying on the discount.

red_flags: China EDA export-control exposure (US restrictions on EDA software sales to Chinese semiconductor customers, partially eased in 2025) is a real revenue-at-risk item
elevated leverage (net debt/EBITDA 3.5x) from debt-funded Ansys acquisition
SNPS.one_line: EDA chip-design software duopolist (with Cadence) now also owns Ansys simulation - near-essential tools for semiconductor design.
SNPS.reason: Revenue/EPS growth is inflated by the Ansys merger and margin is temporarily compressed by deal costs, but the underlying moat (mission-critical, non-substitutable design tools) is as strong as it gets; 24.4x NTM P/E is reasonable once integration and China risk are underwritten, so it merits full diligence.

red_flags: negative profit margin/ROE - likely a GAAP artifact from the Trimble/AGCO precision-ag joint-venture deconsolidation rather than core operating losses; unverified
TRMB.one_line: Positioning/GPS hardware and software for construction, agriculture and transportation, now restructured around 50/50 JVs.
TRMB.reason: Scores don't clear the bar (quality/growth both mid-pack) even though the cheap multiple and JV-driven margin distortion look like they may be overstating the weakness; not disqualified, just not compelling enough to advance this round.

TYL.one_line: Dominant public-sector software (courts, property tax/appraisal, ERP) for US state and local governments.
TYL.reason: Multi-decade government contracts create extreme switching costs; steady 8.2% revenue growth plus SaaS-transition margin inflection at 22.1x NTM P/E (well below Tyler's historical premium) makes this a clear advance.

WDAY.one_line: HCM/financials SaaS suite for large enterprises with sticky, hard-to-rip-out payroll and HR systems.
WDAY.reason: Solid but unremarkable across the board: growth has slowed to 12.8%, and only 10.2% street upside signals limited analyst conviction; doesn't clear quality>=4 or growth>=4, so it stays in the pile for now rather than advancing.

red_flags: customer concentration (Meta and Microsoft are large single-digit-to-double-digit-percent customers)
competitive risk from hyperscaler in-house silicon and Nvidia's networking push
ANET.one_line: AI/cloud data-center networking leader (EOS software moat) for hyperscalers.
ANET.reason: 37.7% revenue growth with 38% margins and 31.5% ROE is a rare combination; 42x NTM P/E is full but not absurd given the multi-year AI-networking capex cycle, so this warrants full diligence despite customer-concentration risk.

red_flags: stock up ~163% over 12 months - valuation and expectations are extended; AI-datacenter-interconnect capex cycle could normalize
CIEN.one_line: Optical networking/coherent-optics equipment maker riding the AI datacenter interconnect buildout.
CIEN.reason: 37% revenue growth and thin FCF yield (1.3%) are typical of a capital-intensive equipment cycle; street still sees 44.8% upside even after the huge run, so the growth case survives the momentum, but this needs a hard look at cycle durability before sizing.

CSCO.one_line: Legacy networking incumbent (switches/routers) reaccelerating via AI-networking demand and Splunk/security cross-sell.
CSCO.reason: 17.6% revenue growth (reaccelerating from a multi-year lull) with 27% ROE and a 1.6% dividend at a reasonable 20.4x NTM P/E is an attractive combination for an incumbent with a huge installed base.

FFIV.one_line: Application-delivery and security appliances/software (load balancers, WAF) for enterprise data centers.
FFIV.reason: Growth is modest (10.9%) and, critically, the street target implies -1.6% downside from here - analysts already see the stock as fully to over-valued, so price_vs_growth fails outright.

red_flags: reported profit margin/ROE deeply negative - needs verification whether this is a one-time non-cash charge (e.g., convertible-debt or impairment item) versus genuine cash losses
stock up ~460% over 12 months on AI-optics mania
LITE.one_line: Optical components/laser maker riding the AI datacenter transceiver (800G/1.6T) upgrade cycle.
LITE.reason: 109% revenue growth is a real AI-capex tailwind, but a nearly 5x run in twelve months at 38x NTM P/E on a barely-positive FCF yield (0.3%) means the price already assumes the supercycle continues without interruption; too extended to chase, and the negative margin needs cleaning up before any real conclusion.

MSI.one_line: Near-monopoly US public-safety radio/911-dispatch/video-security provider (P25 land-mobile radio, Avigilon).
MSI.reason: Multi-decade, mission-critical government contracts are about as durable a moat as exists in tech; steady 13.3% growth and a high (buyback-driven) ROE at 24.1x NTM P/E is a fair price for that quality, so this clears the bar on quality alone.

APH.one_line: Interconnect/sensor leader (connectors, cable assemblies) and serial acquirer across AI datacenter, auto, defense and broadband.
APH.reason: 55% revenue growth (organic plus disciplined M&A) with 38% ROE is best-in-class; FCF yield is temporarily low from AI-driven capex, but the long capital-allocation track record and diversified end-market exposure make this a strong advance.

red_flags: negative FCF yield (-1.1%) despite a huge share-price run (+158% in 12 months) - cash conversion needs to catch up to the reported earnings recovery
COHR.one_line: Photonics/laser and optical-components maker (merged II-VI/Coherent) turning around into an AI-optics transceiver supplier.
COHR.reason: 34% revenue growth and a strong EPS recovery support the turnaround narrative and 40% street upside, but negative free cash flow alongside the rally is a real caution flag that full diligence needs to resolve before sizing conviction.

GLW.one_line: Materials-science leader (Gorilla Glass, optical fiber) riding an AI-datacenter fiber upgrade cycle ("Springboard" plan).
GLW.reason: Good business but already fully re-rated: stock up 83% in a year to 38.5x NTM P/E against a near-zero FCF yield (0.5%) - much of the AI-fiber upside looks priced in already; better to revisit on a pullback.

red_flags: cyclical: current growth partly reflects a semiconductor/AI test-capex upswing that could moderate
KEYS.one_line: Test-and-measurement equipment/software leader (semiconductor, telecom, aerospace/defense validation).
KEYS.reason: 36.5% revenue growth reflects a real cyclical recovery plus AI/6G test-capex tailwinds, with a durable duopoly-like moat; 26.6x NTM P/E is fair for the cycle, so this merits full diligence on durability.

red_flags: forward EPS growth guide is nearly flat (+1.3%) - confirm whether this reflects deal-integration/portfolio-transition timing (recent divestitures being redeployed into new SaaS M&A) rather than a genuine deceleration
ROP.one_line: Diversified vertical-market software conglomerate (permitting, insurance, medical, network software) built by disciplined M&A.
ROP.reason: 90%+ recurring revenue and a best-in-class capital-allocation record justify quality=4; 15.1x NTM P/E is unusually cheap for Roper (historically 20-25x) with a 6.4% FCF yield, but the flat near-term EPS guide needs to be understood before concluding this is simply cheap.

TDY.one_line: Diversified instrumentation, sensors, defense and digital-imaging company built by disciplined serial acquisition.
TDY.reason: Consistent 9.8% revenue growth and 29% EPS growth at a reasonable 23.4x NTM P/E, with a long history of disciplined capital allocation across niche, high-switching-cost end markets - a steady compounder worth full diligence.

red_flags: hardware-heavy, cyclical business - current growth partly reflects rebound from 2023 retail/warehouse inventory destocking
ZBRA.one_line: Barcode scanning/RFID and rugged mobile-computing leader for retail and warehouse/logistics.
ZBRA.reason: 20.4% revenue growth and a sharp margin snapback (103% EPS growth) at a reasonable 16.9x NTM P/E clears the growth bar; already ranks well in the quant model too, so worth confirming the cyclical recovery has legs.

red_flags: core EMS business is inherently low-margin/commoditized; monitor whether the data-center power/cooling mix shift (JetCool) is durable or just riding the current AI capex wave
FLEX.one_line: Electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider increasingly mixed toward AI-datacenter power and liquid-cooling systems.
FLEX.reason: 20.6% revenue growth and a real margin-mix shift toward higher-value datacenter power/cooling support 40% street upside at 19.5x NTM P/E; growth clears the bar despite EMS's traditionally thin, cyclical margins.

red_flags: thin core EMS margins (2.6%); high ROE partly reflects a small equity base from buybacks rather than pure business quality
JBL.one_line: Electronics manufacturing services provider with growing AI-datacenter infrastructure (power, cooling, networking) exposure.
JBL.reason: 11.8% revenue growth and 111% EPS growth from AI-related mix shift, at 18.8x NTM P/E with 36% street upside, clears the growth bar; worth a closer look at how much of the earnings power is capex-cycle-dependent.

TEL.one_line: Diversified connector/sensor leader across auto, industrial, AI datacenter, and aerospace/defense end markets.
TEL.reason: 13.8% revenue growth and 26.5% EPS growth with disciplined capital allocation and diversified exposure at a reasonable 16.9x NTM P/E is a solid quality-driven advance.

red_flags: US federal government segment revenue pressure from 2025 federal budget/efficiency-driven contract reviews and terminations
long-run risk that GenAI reduces demand/pricing for traditional staff-augmentation consulting, even as ACN also sells GenAI integration work
ACN.one_line: Global #1 IT/management consulting and systems-integration franchise, now repositioning around GenAI "reinvention" services.
ACN.reason: Growth has genuinely slowed to 5.6% amid federal-government headwinds, but an 11.2% FCF yield and 12x NTM P/E (down from Accenture's historical 25-30x) is priced for far more pessimism than the franchise quality and net-cash balance sheet likely warrant; already model_rank 50 and v1-flagged attractive, so full diligence should focus on how much of the federal/GenAI risk is already reflected.

red_flags: same GenAI/staff-augmentation cannibalization risk as ACN, with less diversification and a heavier health-insurance/payer client concentration
CTSH.one_line: Mid-tier IT services/BPO provider with a large health-insurance and payer client base, under a multi-year turnaround.
CTSH.reason: Cheap (9.3x NTM P/E, 8.2% FCF yield) but growth is slow (4.5%) and quality/moat is a notch below peers like Accenture; doesn't clear the quality>=4 or growth>=4 bar, so it's a pass for now rather than a value trap bet.

IBM.one_line: Hybrid-cloud (Red Hat), AI (watsonx) and consulting company still carrying a large legacy mainframe/services base.
IBM.reason: Revenue growth is essentially flat (1.1%) and the street sees only 6.7% upside; earnings growth is buyback/margin-driven rather than organic, so this doesn't clear the growth or quality bar despite a fair price.

red_flags: revenue growth is negative (-0.6%) for a subscription research/advisory business that has compounded contract-value growth for two decades - consistent with reported concerns that GenAI is reducing willingness-to-pay for traditional IT-research subscriptions and that enterprise IT-budget pressure is hitting Gartner's consulting/conference segments
street target implies -1.5% downside
IT.one_line: IT research and advisory subscription business (Gartner for IT leaders) plus consulting and conferences.
IT.reason: A two-decade compounder now showing outright revenue decline and a street target below the current price is a genuine secular-disruption warning sign, not just a cheap multiple; disqualifying red flag, so reject despite the historically strong moat.

red_flags: elevated leverage (net debt/EBITDA 5.5x) mid-transition
legacy CDN business (~40% of revenue) is structurally declining/commoditizing, offset by growing security and cloud-compute segments
AKAM.one_line: Legacy CDN provider transitioning toward security (WAAP/segmentation) and cloud compute (Linode), which now drive most of the growth.
AKAM.reason: The transition story is real and the stock is cheap (16.7x NTM P/E, 38.8% street upside), but blended growth is still modest (5.4%) and leverage is elevated for a company mid-transition; doesn't clear quality>=4 or growth>=4, so pass for now and revisit as the security/cloud mix keeps improving.
